analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only changes in docs/provider/cli-reference.md, so no executable code or security control changes. The change documents a new waitlist gate for `darkbloom sandbox setup` (lines 1360-1381) and `darkbloom cluster` on a Mac with no pairing (lines 1708-1727), plus a new `darkbloom waitlist` command section (1636-1706). The gate is a coordinator-side GET /v1/waitlists/sandbox call using the login token; the join is POST with body `{}` and sends nothing about the Mac. The documented client-side safeguards are: HTTPS or loopback-HTTP only, no redirects, 10 s timeout, 64 KiB response cap, and control/format/bidi characters in coordinator text printed as U+FFFD (1686-1690). Those are good mitigations for terminal injection from an untrusted coordinator response.

The security-relevant points for the integration pass are these. The waitlist is a product-access gate and not a security boundary: a `404` or an unreadable answer is treated as 'going on' for 404 only, while other failures stop setup. A malicious or MITM'd 404 therefore skips the gate, but the gate is not an authorization control. The T-061 installer download path (TB-013) is unchanged: TLS-only, 1 MiB cap, `#!` check, 0600 script in a 0700 dir, and the CLI does not verify the script beyond TLS (1409-1411). The doc states the installer verifies the add-on release itself. I could not verify the implementation (SandboxSetupCommand.swift, FeatureWaitlistGate.swift, WaitlistCommand.swift) because only the docs were supplied, so I cannot confirm the documented sanitization, redirect refusal or size caps actually exist in code. The SDK 27.2 Date-comparison note (1773-1783) matches the A-018 availability item in the context and introduces no new behavior. The head ranges in the unit are doc text only; no threat model assets are weakened. I identified no regression. Remaining question: whether the code that is separately changed in the PR implements the documented bounds, which this pass could not check.
